question: What mistakes does a profile make when every prompt may rewrite it?
why: Mickey's three arms (23:10 to 24:37) and "remember everything, see what mistakes it makes". The aggressive arm is the one whose mistakes are the result.
source: wiki/meta/spec-2026-11-10-la-personalization-lab-test-tree.md, heading "Aspect `aggressiveness`: none, light or aggressive?", row `aggressive`
hypothesis: Every prompt may rewrite the profile: it fills by turn 2 and flips on outliers; useful as the "what mistakes it makes" arm.
cost_estimate: about 0.5M Haiku tokens (the test tree's estimate); one typed call per turn on the 20-persona sample and syn1, about 185 calls per run, 3 runs

deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); Amendment A2 maps the row: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas, and the real1 extras (fill_rate_at_k, run_agreement, flips_per_10_turns) are computed on the same anon-personas runs, numbers only. As a model case it runs the A2 seeded sample of anon-personas, the same one as reverify/heldout-personas: sample_dataset anon-personas, sample_size 20, sample_seed 20261110, random.Random(seed).sample(sorted(user_ids), 20). syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside, never alone.
deviations.labels: Labels on anon-personas were written by headless Claude and are not human-reviewed (A2, decision 1): every verdict carries the caveat 'labels not human-reviewed'.
deviations.agg: The row says `turns_to_fill` median <= 2. The kit's aggregations are mean, min, max, pooled and each, and the metric is itself a median over slots, so the bar reads the mean of the three runs' medians (agg mean); the bar value is not loosened. first_session_fill names no aggregation: default mean.
deviations.no_bar: outlier_flips, flips_per_10_turns and wrong_slot_turns are reported with no bar (the mistakes are the result). fill_rate_at_k (k = 2, 4, 8) and run_agreement are the real1 extras, reported with no bar.
deviations.arm: min_support 1, ratio 0.0: the latest confident signal wins (P/arms.py, ArmUpdater); no nightly job, so the arms differ only in their update rule.
